first_principles_point: Healthcare access is the hard distance between medical need and paid care.
money_path: medical need -> permission -> capacity -> delivery -> claim -> reimbursement -> cash -> quality/trust test
company_examples: UnitedHealth; Cigna; DaVita; Addus; Option Care; BrightSpring; Enhabit
proof_needed: authorization; staffing; reimbursement; claims; receivables; OCF; quality
safe_use: Safe claim: healthcare access is a conversion system, not mere demand.

first_principles_point: A sick or aging patient does not become revenue until care is reachable, authorized, staffed, delivered, billed, and paid.
money_path: patient need -> provider/payer route -> appointment or authorization -> delivered care -> claim -> payment
company_examples: UnitedHealth; Cigna; DaVita; Addus; Option Care; CVS; Humana; HCA
proof_needed: patients served; appointments; authorizations; claims; payer mix; cash collection
safe_use: Safe claim: need creates pressure, not proof of delivered care.

first_principles_point: Payers and PBMs control networks, authorization, claims, pharmacy routing, and medical-cost risk.
money_path: premium or fee -> payer/PBM -> network/authorization/claims/pharmacy route -> cost and earnings -> cash
proof_needed: medical cost ratio; claims payable; premium receivables; segment margin; retention; OCF
safe_use: Safe claim: payer scale is routing power, but not proof of fair access.

first_principles_point: Drugs become care only when prescribed, covered, dispensed, delivered, reimbursed, and taken.
money_path: therapy need -> prescription/referral -> authorization -> pharmacy/specialty route -> claim -> reimbursement
company_examples: Cigna/Evernorth; CVS/Caremark; OptumRx; McKesson; Cencora; Option Care; BrightSpring
proof_needed: script volume; specialty mix; rebates/regulatory risk; inventory; receivables; margin
safe_use: Safe claim: pharmacy routing is infrastructure, not automatic affordability proof.

first_principles_point: Aging and chronic disease move care into homes, senior housing, hospice, home health, infusion, and equipment logistics.
money_path: aging/chronic need -> home-care referral -> caregiver/nurse/equipment/drug route -> reimbursed visit/service -> cash after wages
company_examples: Addus; BrightSpring; Enhabit; Aveanna; AdaptHealth; Welltower; Ventas; Option Care
proof_needed: census; visits; billable hours; reimbursement rates; caregiver retention; receivables
safe_use: Safe claim: aging supports demand, but worker and reimbursement math decide cash.

first_principles_point: Healthcare labor is not just expense; it is the capacity to deliver the product.
money_path: care need -> clinician/caregiver availability -> scheduled service -> wage cost -> reimbursement -> margin
company_examples: Addus; Enhabit; BrightSpring; Aveanna; HCA; DaVita; Option Care
proof_needed: staffing ratios; billable hours; wage rates; hiring; retention; labor productivity
safe_use: Safe claim: labor shortage can raise value or destroy margin.

first_principles_point: Chronic conditions create repeated care routes, but repeated volume is not quality or cash proof.
money_path: chronic condition -> repeated treatment schedule -> staffed center/home model -> claim per treatment -> reimbursement -> cash
company_examples: DaVita; Fresenius; UnitedHealth kidney care; chronic-care operators
proof_needed: treatments; revenue per treatment; cost per treatment; payer mix; utilization; outcomes
safe_use: Safe claim: recurring care creates density, not automatic good economics.

first_principles_point: Screening turns hidden risk into tests, diagnoses, referrals, and downstream care routes.
money_path: risk/symptom -> test order -> lab/device workflow -> coverage/payment -> result -> treatment/referral
company_examples: Labcorp; Quest; Natera; Exact Sciences; Abbott; Thermo Fisher; Hologic
proof_needed: test volume; reimbursement; payer coverage; false positives; downstream care; outcomes
safe_use: Safe claim: diagnostics can open care pathways, but volume is not clinical value proof.

first_principles_point: Patients cannot easily judge medical quality, so trusted routes have economic value.
money_path: vulnerable patient need -> trusted route -> appointment/test/treatment/fill -> continued use/referral -> cash
company_examples: UnitedHealth; Cigna; HCA; Labcorp; Quest; DaVita; Option Care; trusted care brands
proof_needed: retention; referrals; quality scores; complaints; denials; adherence; outcomes
safe_use: Safe claim: trust matters economically, but scale or brand is not proof of trust.

first_principles_point: Reimbursement quality decides whether access becomes cash after payer rules, rates, coding, and denials.
money_path: covered service -> coded claim -> payer adjudication -> allowed amount -> payment timing -> cash collection
company_examples: UnitedHealth; Cigna; DaVita; Addus; Option Care; HCA; McKesson; Cencora
proof_needed: payer mix; rates; denials; receivable aging; claim collections; medical cost ratio
safe_use: Safe claim: revenue needs reimbursement and collection support.

first_principles_point: Healthcare can look healthy in revenue while cash is tied up in drugs, claims, receivables, wages, or inventory.
money_path: service/drug cost -> claim or bill -> receivable/claims payable -> payment lag -> operating cash flow
company_examples: Option Care; Cigna; UnitedHealth; McKesson; Cencora; DaVita; Addus; hospitals
proof_needed: inventory; receivables; claims payable; DSO; OCF; FCF; debt
safe_use: Safe claim: cash quality requires balance sheet and cash-flow evidence.

first_principles_point: Families provide coordination labor that company accounts often do not capture.
money_path: patient need -> family coordination -> formal provider/payer route -> reimbursed care -> unpaid burden remains
company_examples: home care; hospice; senior housing; chronic care; infusion; dialysis
proof_needed: caregiver burden; visit gaps; coordination measures; patient support; complaints
safe_use: Safe claim: company revenue omits some social cost.

first_principles_point: The proof ladder runs from demand to access to reimbursement to operating conversion to trust and cash proof.
money_path: demand -> access -> reimbursement -> operating conversion -> claims/receipts/outcomes/trust
proof_needed: covered lives; patients; claims; receivables; OCF; quality; outcomes; denial data
safe_use: Safe claim: most current evidence is levels 1-4 in pieces; level 5 remains open.

first_principles_point: Each healthcare model needs its own proof standard: payer, PBM, dialysis, home care, infusion, hospital, lab, device, and distributor.
money_path: company type -> correct healthcare metric -> cash-quality bridge -> safe claim or gap
company_examples: UnitedHealth; Cigna; DaVita; Addus; Option Care; BrightSpring; HCA; Labcorp
proof_needed: model-specific metrics; segment data; reimbursement; labor; cash flow; quality
safe_use: Safe claim: no one generic healthcare metric proves the whole theme.

first_principles_point: The central question is whether companies reduce patient burden or simply control the route through which burden passes.
money_path: vulnerability -> administrative route -> access or friction -> company revenue -> patient/family outcome
company_examples: payers; providers; PBMs; home-care operators; diagnostics; hospitals
proof_needed: denials; quality; satisfaction; outcomes; affordability; labor adequacy; complaints
safe_use: Safe claim: healthcare access is both an economic and social burden-transfer system.

first_principles_point: The next proof pass must go below revenue into claims, receivables, payer mix, labor, drug cost, quality, and cash conversion.
money_path: source pull -> service-line table -> claim/reimbursement bridge -> cash-quality and outcome boundary
company_examples: UnitedHealth; Cigna; DaVita; Addus; Option Care
proof_needed: MCR; claims payable; receivables; payer mix; rates; billable hours; drug inventory; OCF; quality
safe_use: Safe claim: this page defines the next cash-quality extraction path; it is not extraction itself.
